seoTitle: Free Kubernetes YAML Manifest Validator Online
metaDescription: Lint Kubernetes YAML for wrong apiVersion and kind pairs, invalid names, selector mismatches, :latest images, missing probes and privileged mode.
intro: Paste one or more Kubernetes manifests and get a structural check of apiVersion, names, selectors, images, resources, probes and privileged settings.
why:
Most broken manifests fail for ordinary reasons: a Deployment selector that does not match the pod template labels, an apiVersion that was removed in a newer cluster, an uppercase character in a name, or an image with no tag. kubectl tells you only after you apply, and sometimes only as a vague message.

This validator reads multi-document YAML as text and checks those common mistakes, plus risky settings such as privileged containers, hostNetwork and root users. It is a structural lint based on indentation and patterns, not a schema validator, so it cannot know every kind. Use kubectl apply --dry-run=server or kubeconform for authoritative checks.
howTo: Paste your Kubernetes YAML, separating documents with a line of three dashes.
Read the findings, which are labelled ERROR, WARNING or INFO with a document number.
Fix the manifest, then confirm it with kubectl apply --dry-run=server.

faq.q: Is this a full schema validation?
faq.a: No. It checks a fixed list of common problems for about twenty built-in kinds using patterns. For schema-level validation of any resource, use kubeconform or a server-side dry run.

faq.q: Does it work with flow-style YAML?
faq.a: Only partly. The checks follow indentation, so manifests written with inline braces such as {app: web} are not fully analysed. Convert them to block style first.

faq.q: What does the selector check do?
faq.a: For Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets and ReplicaSets it compares each matchLabels pair with the pod template labels and reports any that do not match.
